subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Gunpowder Tea
description: Learn Gunpowder Tea in one minute.

hook.text: Gunpowder tea leaves are rolled into tiny, tight pellets that look like lead shot from an old musket.

buildup.text: Rolling compresses the leaf, slowing oxidation and locking in freshness for longer storage and transport.

discovery.text: When steeped, the pellets unfurl dramatically. One teaspoon produces more flavor than you'd expect.

twist.text: Gunpowder tea is the base for Moroccan mint tea—mixed with fresh spearmint and generous amounts of sugar.

climax.text: This pellet format was invented for export in the 1600s. It traveled better than loose leaves on long sea voyages.

punchline.text: Tiny pellets, big flavor, built to travel. That's gunpowder tea.

quiz.question: Why were gunpowder tea leaves rolled into pellets?
options: To slow oxidation and improve durability for transport

details.summary: Gunpowder tea gets its name from its tightly rolled pellet shape, which resembles old musket gunpowder. This Chinese green tea has a bold, slightly smoky flavor and is the base for North African mint tea. The rolling preserves freshness, giving gunpowder tea a long shelf life.
details.whyItMatters: Gunpowder tea bridges Chinese tea tradition and North African culture, demonstrating how a single tea can take on vastly different cultural meanings across continents.
takeaways: Leaves are rolled into tight pellets resembling gunpowder
It is the traditional base for Moroccan mint tea
Tight rolling preserves freshness for extended storage

faq.question: Why is gunpowder tea used in Moroccan mint tea?
faq.answer: Gunpowder's bold, slightly bitter flavor balances the sweetness of the generous sugar added in North African preparation. Its compact shape made it ideal for the long caravan trade routes from China to Morocco. The tradition dates back centuries and remains central to Moroccan hospitality.

faq.question: How do you brew gunpowder tea properly?
faq.answer: Use water at about 80 degrees Celsius and steep for one to two minutes. The pellets unfurl dramatically, so use a generous amount of water. For Moroccan style, brew strong with fresh spearmint leaves and sugar. The tea can handle two to three resteeps.
